MAJOR: `main()` still calls `backlog.get_epic()` for the single-item path and then `evaluate(a.item)` re-fetches the item independently; the rendered design pack can be produced from a different store snapshot than the one validated (integrity gap) and duplicates the read on every invocation.

`_validate_cfg` checks only `enforce_from`; other config defects (e.g. `enforce_items` not a list, unparseable content) still fall through to `should_enforce`/`enforce_items` logic unchecked, so the fail-open class of bug the guard targets is only partially closed.
MINOR: On a config problem, `evaluate()` short-circuits and drops all item-scoped date diagnostics, so a run reports config errors but hides created_at/enforce_items defects — operators must iterate to see the full problem set (observability).
`test_evaluate_validates_config_once` uses `f"design_pack_cfg_{1}.json"` — a placeholder f-string that reads like copy-paste; the intent (unique temp cfg path) should be self-evident.
`main()` ignores the `item` dict it fetched; the local is now dead except for the falsy `{}` default, which makes the control flow misleading for maintainers.
NIT: The new whitespace case (`"2026-10-05 "`) is appended to an existing test rather than given its own test, weakening failure isolation and making the regression intent hard to discover.

`test_parse_date_accepts_date_and_datetime` implicitly pins the ≥3.11 `datetime.fromisoformat` date-only behavior via a passing test only on the CI interpreter; no comment or marker documents the interpreter requirement the prior finding flagged.
SUMMARY: Prior fail-open and coverage gaps are genuinely addressed: config validation now lives in `evaluate()`, the `--item` path routes through it, and tests cover missing `enforce_from`, whitespace, and date-only parsing.

Remaining risk is the duplicated, potentially divergent item fetch in `main()` (validation vs. render can see different snapshots) and the partial scope of the config guard, which still leaves other malformed config fields unchecked.
Diff is a net improvement and close to acceptable; clean up the double fetch and broaden `_validate_cfg` before merge.
